She complained about damp and mould in the children's bedroom. On 21 January 2024, the resident complained about worsening damp and mould in a bedroom over the past year, claiming it was making her children sick and damaging her belongings. She said that a specialist visited on 23 October 2023, she never received a copy of the report, and no repairs were done. She said that no one responded when she tried to follow up. On 5 February 2024, the landlord sent its stage 1 complaint response, acknowledging taking no action despite the resident's follow-ups and apologised. It said it would conduct an urgent mould wash, install a kitchen extractor fan and instruct a surveyor to find the root cause. It offered £430 compensation for time and inconvenience. On 23 February 2024, the resident asked the landlord to escalate the complaint due to poor communication and a missed response deadline. She thought the problem might have been coming from the downstairs flat and rejected its compensation offer as it failed to complete promised actions. She repeated concerns about her children's health. The resident asked the Ombudsman to investigate, stating that although the mould was treated, the root cause remained unresolved. She told us that she moved her children out of the affected room and now sleeps in there herself. She said the situation was causing stress, and she wanted further compensation.

partial_case.facts: The resident lives in a 2-bedroom first-floor flat with her children; the landlord knew that one child has asthma, and she complained about damp and mould in the children’s bedroom. On 21 January 2024, the resident complained about worsening damp and mould in a bedroom over the past year, said it was making her children sick and damaging belongings, and said a specialist had visited on 23 October 2023 but she had not received the report and no repairs had been done. On 5 February 2024, the landlord sent its stage 1 response, saying the inspection found acceptable damp levels but extensive mould on the bedroom wall requiring treatment, noting no kitchen extractor fan, apologising for no action despite follow-ups, proposing an urgent mould wash, extractor fan installation and a surveyor visit, and offering £430 compensation. On 23 February 2024, the resident asked to escalate the complaint because of poor communication and a missed response deadline, suspected the issue might be coming from the downstairs flat, rejected the compensation offer because promised actions had not been completed, and repeated concerns about her children’s health. In the referral to the Ombudsman, the resident said that although the mould had been treated, the root cause remained unresolved; she said she had moved her children out of the affected room, slept there herself, experienced stress, and wanted further compensation.

determinations.issue: Reports of damp and mould in a bedroom

orders.action: The landlord must pay the resident £50 to recognise distress and inconvenience caused by its handling of the complaint.

recommendations.action: The reasonable redress finding for damp and mould was made on the basis that the landlord pays the resident £1,080 offered on 10 April 2024, if not already paid.
The landlord should arrange a survey to assess the property, including ongoing damp, and identify any repairs it is responsible for.

There was service failure for the landlord’s handling of the complaint.

This indicates poor record keeping and likely caused confusion.
The landlord failed to apologise for any delays or offer any redress for its complaint handling failures. We have made an order to reflect this.
